newsitem.title: UK: US Stocks in London up, braced for payrolls data.
newsitem.headline: US Stocks in London up, braced for payrolls data.

text.p: U.S. shares trading in London were slightly higher on Thursday in thin trade as investors awaited the key June employment report at 1230 GMT.

"We're seeing a slight upward bias ahead of the long (Independence Day holiday) weekend," said one trader. "Providing there's no major upset from the payrolls data we should see a firmer opening in the States."

U.S. stocks staged a fierce rally late on Wednesday after the Fed left interest rates unchanged following the regular FOMC meeting, as expected. The Dow rose 73.05 pts or 0.95 percent to 7795.98, stopping just one point short of its all-time high.
But the market was also squeezed higher on position squaring ahead of today's release of the June employment report.

Analysts expect non-farm payrolls to rise by around 222,000 in June, following a previous monthly rise of 138,000. The unemployment rate was expected to remain steady at 4.8 percent whilst average hourly earnings were seen nudging up by 0.4 percent.
Among individual share movers in London, the only sector that bucked the firmer trend was pharmaceuticals, after Pharmacia & Upjohn which is not traded in London, warned on second quarter profits.
Pharmacia closed at $276.5 in New York. In London, Merck was down $3/8 at $104-1/4 and Pfizer came off $3/8 to $62-1/8.

"The market is still looking unstoppable," said one dealer. "We have second quarter earnings coming up next week but the market is aware that they may be disappointing and doesn't seem to be too worried.
"The feeling is that earnings will pick up again later in the year," he added.

Elsewhere, food stocks were benefiting from the decision by General Mills Inc to raise cereal prices by an average of 2.6 percent. Campbell Soup was up $1/4 to $47-7/8 and CPC International was up $3/8 at $94-1/8.
Shares in Philip Morris were encouraged by overnight press comment on continuing litigation. The shares gained $1/8 to $44-1/8.
Hi-techs and auto's also featured, dealers said.

Texas Instruments was up $3/8 to $88-3/8 following news that Raytheon Co's acquisition of its defence system and electronics unit had been approved as long as Raytheon sells a key chip-making operation.
Intel put on $1/4 to $143-1/4 and IBM was up $3/8 to $93-7/8.
